description: The permission set the main window runs under, audited against what the interface actually calls. The frontend imports three things from @tauri-apps/api: invoke (hayat/jisr.ts), listen (shashat/luba.tsx, shashat/warsha.tsx) and getCurrentWindow (hayat/nafidha.ts). listen is one of two core modules the interface drives, and the unlisten half is used, so core:event:allow-listen and core:event:allow-unlisten are named here even though core:default already implies them; naming them is the record of who consumes them. The other is the window: on Windows the product declines the platform frame (tauri.windows.conf.json sets decorations false) and draws its own strip, so it holds exactly the six window grants that strip needs — start-dragging and internal-toggle-maximize for the drag region Tauri's own script drives from data-tauri-drag-region, minimize, toggle-maximize and close for the three controls, and is-maximized so the middle control shows the right glyph after onResized. Nothing else about the window is granted: no set-title, no set-size, no position, no always-on-top. Progress events are emitted from Rust through tauri::Emitter, never from the webview, so no emit grant is held either. The build's version and name reach the interface through the maalumat_taarib command, not core:app. core:webview:allow-internal-toggle-devtools is retained because it cannot be withdrawn from here: it is a member of core:webview:default and therefore of core:default, and a Capability at tauri 2.11.5 has no debug-only or profile field to scope it with — only platforms, whose values are operating systems. The real gate is the tauri devtools cargo feature; see docs/tawzee/adhonat.md. One plugin permission is held: opener:allow-open-url, scoped to https://** and nothing else, for the opener plugin the game screen's community-translation panel relies on. The interface does not call the plugin's command itself — it calls Taarib's iftah_rabt, which refuses anything that is not an https address on a host the community index links to or a known mod platform before the plugin sees it — and the scope is the second fence behind the first: were the plugin's command ever invoked from the webview, nothing but an https page could open, and no file or path could. No open-path and no reveal-item-in-dir grant is held. Nothing here grants filesystem, shell or network access. Those go through Taarib's own commands, which are not governed by this file at all and are validated against taarib_usus::masarat before they touch the machine.
